overview.text: A square is a four-sided polygon with four equal sides and four right angles. It is distinctive because it belongs to several familiar quadrilateral families at once: it is both a rectangle, with four right angles, and a rhombus, with four equal sides; it is also a parallelogram and a regular polygon. This makes it a useful geometric model: its equal sides and right angles connect ideas about length, area, and perimeter in a particularly simple shape. If a side has length s, its area is s² and its perimeter is 4s. Its diagonals also have predictable relationships that help describe or calculate its dimensions.

key_facts.text: A square is simultaneously a rectangle, a rhombus, a parallelogram, and a regular polygon.
For side length s, the perimeter is 4s and the area is s².
The two diagonals are equal; each bisects the other, and they meet at right angles.
A square’s diagonal has length s√2 when its side length is s.
A square is a regular quadrilateral: all four sides are equal and all four angles are equal.
